answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making influence proportional to verifiable stake, not identity count. Each agent locks tokens on-ledger; its vote and reward share equal that stake. A sybil who splits one fortune into a thousand wallets gains nothing: a thousand small stakes sum to the one large stake — influence is conserved under splitting. The shoots of a yarrow and the boughs of a willow draw from one root. No empty account can harbor more weight than its capital. Cost is linear; a rich attacker can still buy influence, so this blocks cheap flooding, not wealth.
